I have farmed this land for 25 years. I never went to school, but I know every corner of my 24 mu in Quzhou County. My son works in the city now, so it is just me and my husband at home. We have a well for water.

I put 16 mu into the wheat-maize rotation because that is what our land is good for, and I keep 8 mu for cotton. Cotton brings more cash, but it is more work and needs more attention.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the same shop every year — the same kind my neighbor Old Wang plants. After the maize comes off in autumn, I hire the rotary tiller to turn the ground. I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, 50 kilos, before tilling. Then in March, when the wheat starts greening up, I spread almost a full bag of urea, about 40 kilos per mu. I have done this for ten years. If Old Wang adds an extra half-bag, I add it too. I water three times: once before winter so the wheat does not freeze, once when the stems start growing fast, and once when the heads come out. I spray pesticide twice — once for grass and once when I see insects eating the leaves. If the weather is normal, I should get about 450 kilos per mu.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed right after cutting the wheat in June. There is no time to plough again, so I plant directly into the stubble — no-tillage. I put one bag of compound fertilizer, 50 kilos per mu, into the holes when planting. When the corn is knee-high, I spread half a bag of urea, 25 kilos per mu. I water twice: once right after planting if the ground is dry, and once when the tassels come out. I spray twice: herbicide at planting, and one more time for armyworms later. I expect about 550 kilos per mu.

For cotton, I plant hybrid cotton on 8 mu in April. I rotary till first to break up the soil. Cotton is hungry. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu, 100 kilos total, as base. Then I add one full bag of urea, 50 kilos per mu, half at budding and half at flowering. I water three times: at budding, at flowering, and when the bolls are forming. I spray four times. Last year the red spiders came late and cost me money, so this year I will spray four times to be safe, even if it costs more. I hope for 260 kilos of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive this year, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I would rather put one extra bag than risk losing the crop. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone on this side of the village applies a certain amount, I do the same. I do not change what works, and I do not trust new ideas unless I saw them work on someone else's field first.
